Theme

Body, health & movement

gallop verb and noun

also at a gallop, canter

classical

Caes. BC 3.96; Liv. 1.27.7: citātō equō, at full gallop (Lewis & Short s.v. citō)

citātō equō

at a gallop

The classical way to say a rider gallops, beside a verb of motion.

Other words

  • quadrupedō, quadrupedāre — gallop (Traupman’s verb)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 320

    Lewis & Short calls the verb obsolete: only its participle quadrupedāns, galloping, is found (Plaut. Capt. 4.2.34; Verg. A. 8.596; Plin. NH 8.70.182, Lewis & Short), poetic and post-Augustan.

  • cursus citātus — a gallop

    also used · modern · Traupman 320

    citātus, quick, is classical (Lewis & Short). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

See also horse.
